title: AI Use Guard: shadow-AI visibility and AI-policy records for small firms
source: Top 25 SaaS ideas for Victor (research report, Nov 2026)
summary: Shows which AI tools a company's staff use, warns before someone pastes client data into them, and records AI-policy and training sign-offs. Sold per user, mainly through MSPs.
hook: "I have no idea which AI tools my staff use, or what client data they paste into them."
story:
**Maria is managing partner of a 35-person accounting firm in Stockholm.** Her staff use ChatGPT, Copilot and a few AI note-takers. Nobody approved them, and nobody knows what client data goes in. Last month a large client asked in a supplier questionnaire: **"How do you control the use of AI tools with our data?"** Maria had no answer.

Her IT provider (an MSP) cannot help either: it has **no list of AI tools** in her company. Big-company AI security products are quote-only and made for enterprises. Maria wants a simple view of what is used, a warning before client data is pasted, and a record that everyone signed the AI policy.
whyNow: The EU AI Act's Article 4 "AI literacy" duty has applied since 2 February 2025. The Digital Omnibus, in force since 27 July 2026, softened it to "take measures to support AI literacy", so it is a duty of effort: a conversation opener, not a hard mandate. Meanwhile staff adopt AI faster than firms can control it.
evidence: A Pax8 survey of 1,150 SMB leaders (US, UK, Germany, Sweden) found shadow AI in 35% of AI-using firms, and nearly half got a bigger AI bill than expected [The Next Web]
81% of US SMBs use AI but only 69% have a policy [tech.co]
In large firms, 57% of employees entered confidential information into AI tools and only 24% had mandatory training [Dataconomy]
Only 51.9% of MSPs keep a full inventory of AI tools in client environments [Channel Insider]
Caveat: many shadow-AI percentages cannot be traced to an original study [ainora.lt]

whyReal.title: Staff use AI without asking
whyReal.text: Surveys find shadow AI in about a third of AI-using small firms, and many firms have no written AI policy.

whyReal.title: Clients start asking
whyReal.text: Supplier questionnaires and NIS2 supplier checks now ask how firms handle data in AI tools.

whyReal.title: MSPs have no visibility
whyReal.text: Only about half of MSPs keep a full inventory of AI tools in client environments, so they need a product to offer.

whyReal.title: Enterprise tools left the small market
whyReal.text: SentinelOne bought Prompt Security and Check Point bought Lakera; the rest are quote-based. Small firms have no cheap option.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: Small and mid-sized firms (20–250 staff) in professional services: accounting, law, agencies, recruiting.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: The owner or COO, or the MSP that resells it to its clients.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: MSPs in the EU and English-speaking markets, plus direct sales to EU accounting and law firms.

solution.title: Deploy the extension
solution.text: a Chrome/Edge extension is pushed to all staff through Intune or Google admin.

solution.title: See AI use
solution.text: it detects visits to 200+ AI websites and shows a dashboard per client company.

solution.title: Warn before leaks
solution.text: local pattern-matching spots personal data, IBANs, card numbers and API keys and shows a warning banner (warn, not block, at first).

solution.title: Check connected AI apps
solution.text: a scan of which AI apps users connected to Microsoft 365.

solution.title: Policy and training records
solution.text: an AI-policy generator with employee sign-off, plus 5 short training modules with a completion log.

solution.title: Monthly PDF
solution.text: a report the MSP can use in client reviews.

Victor builds the extension (AI site detection, data-pattern warnings) and the per-client dashboard.

Deploy at pilot MSPs' clients and convert pilots to paid.

risks.risk: Microsoft and Google add native AI data-loss controls
risks.answer: Stay cross-platform and focus on the policy/training records and MSP multi-client view.

risks.risk: Employee-monitoring rules and works councils in the EU
risks.answer: Warn, do not record content; process data locally; give a clear privacy notice.
Sell through MSPs who already push software via Intune or Google admin.
Lead with client questionnaires and data-leak risk, not with the law.

questions: Which AI tools do your (or your clients') staff use for work, and how do you know?
Do you have a written AI usage policy, and is it followed?
Has a client asked how you handle their data in AI tools?
Have you sold any AI-related service yet, and at what price?
Would you deploy a browser extension to all staff, and what would you pay per user?
